narrative.overview: The site is a daily bulletin published by a robot regime. Each date is an issue. Each message is a dispatch from one of two correspondents: the yellow morning robot, who announces the plan, and the red evening robot, who reports how it went. The look is printed on a dark terminal. Monospace type reads like a teletype wire, neon accents read like status lights, and hard rules divide one issue from the next. The joke is the headline story; the chrome is the masthead around it.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black bulletin background with slate panels.
Two robot correspondents in round avatars, yellow (morning) and red (evening).
Cyan for wire and interaction, red for the regime, magenta as a rare glitch accent.
Glow only on what is current or interactive.

rules.name: The Alarm Rule
rules.body: Alarm Red speaks only for the regime: wordmark accent and titles. It never fills a button and never colors message text.

rules.name: The Wire Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element shows Scanline Cyan in at least one state.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Courier New only. Add emphasis with weight, case, and spacing.

rules.name: The Live Wire Rule
rules.body: Glow marks what is current or interactive: today's issue and hovered or focused controls. Back issues in the archive sit flat, with a border and no glow.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Morning cards are amber and evening cards are red. Never style both personas the same way.

dos: Do keep both robot avatars (robot-yellow.jpg for morning, robot-red.jpg for evening). They are binding brand characters.
Do use Courier New for all text, and build hierarchy with weight, case, and spacing.
Do give today's issue Wire Glow, and leave back issues flat.
Do use outlined, square, uppercase controls that fill cyan on hover and focus.
Do keep message text Readout White at 1rem and line-height 1.6 or more, for reading on phones.
Do seal today's evening report until 9:00 PM local time.
donts: Don't use Alarm Red on buttons, links, or message text. It is reserved for the regime's titles and wordmark.
Don't glow everything. A glow on a back issue tells the reader it is new when it isn't.
Don't round controls or navigation. Only cards (4px), panels (12px), and avatars (circle) have curves.
Don't add a second typeface or light-theme surfaces.
Don't nest cards. Issues are sections; only dispatches are cards.
